predecessors.name: Goryeo
predecessors.text: Goryeo, whose throne Yi Seong-gye took in 1392 ('Preceded by: Goryeo; Tamna' in the infobox), without Jeju

predecessors.name: Tamna
predecessors.text: Jeju Island, put under firm central control by Taejong in 1404

successors.name: Korean Empire
successors.text: all of Joseon: 'replaced by the Korean Empire in 1897'; infobox 'Proclamation of the Korean Empire: October 13, 1897'

ledger.x: 1392: Yi Seong-gye is enthroned as King Taejo, founding the Joseon dynasty on Goryeo's land.
1394: the capital moves from Kaegyeong to Hanseong (Seoul).
1399: Jeongjong returns the court to Kaegyeong.
1404: Taejong of Joseon ends the autonomy of Tamna (Jeju).
1405: the court returns to Hanseong for good.
1433: Kim Chongsŏ's campaign pushes the frontier to the Yalu and Tumen.
1592: Hideyoshi's army lands on the south-east coast of Korea.
1593: the Japanese leave Pyongyang and the north.
1627: the Later Jin invades from the north.
1636: the Qing invade and take Hanseong.
1637: Injo surrenders and Joseon becomes a Qing tributary.
1897: the Joseon court proclaims the Korean Empire and Gojong becomes emperor.

wars.name: Ōei Invasion of Tsushima
wars.outcome: Sejong 'launched the punitive Ōei Invasion against Tsushima' in 1419 with 227 ships and some 17,000 soldiers; after 15 days of fighting the lord of Tsushima surrendered.

wars.name: Joseon campaigns against the Jurchens (Four Forts and Six Posts)
wars.outcome: 'In 1433, Kim Chongsŏ's campaign expanded Korean territory, roughly the current border between North Korea and China'; Sejong 'established four forts and six posts' against the Jurchens (no year).

wars.name: Imjin War
wars.outcome: Joseon and Ming victory; 'Status quo ante bellum'.

wars.name: Qing invasion of Joseon
wars.outcome: Qing victory, 9 December 1636 to 30 January 1637; Joseon ended its use of the Ming-era name, sent two princes as hostages, accepted the Qing calendar and paid tribute every year; no land was ceded.

wars.name: First Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: A war 'between Japan and the Qing Empire, fought largely in Korea'; the infobox dates the Japanese occupation to 23 July 1894 and the Treaty of Shimonoseki to 17 April 1895, which 'officially guaranteed Korea's independence from China'.

certainty.note: The northern frontier against the Jurchens is approximate until the 1433 campaign; the south and the coasts are sea frontiers.
The Amnok and Tuman rivers are named as the border but not surveyed; the Jurchen and Ming side of the Changbai mountains was not delimited.

The 1712 Mount Paektu stele set the boundary at the Yalu and Tumen rivers; the Tumen source and the Jiandao shoal north of the river stayed disputed and are the exception (the 1885-1887 talks did not settle it).
